stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor. Let
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor and set
$w = v \circ u$. Denote $q$, resp., $p$ the stalk functor
(\ref{equation-stalk}) associated to $v$, resp.\ $w$.
Then $(u_p\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p$ functorially in the
presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
hypotheses:
Let $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a functor. Let
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor and set
$w = v \circ u$. Denote $q$, resp., $p$ the stalk functor
(\ref{equation-stalk}) associated to $v$, resp.\ $w$.

reason: The stalk of presheaf left Kan extension is a double colimit. Consolidating the colimits and mapping quadruples (V,y,U,φ) to (U,v(φ)y), the proof exhibits a right inverse and connected fibre categories, giving the stalk-colimit identity.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites
given by a continuous functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
Let $q$ be a point of $\mathcal{D}$ given by the functor
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$, see
Definition \ref{definition-point}.
Then the functor $v \circ u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
defines a point $p$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and moreover there is
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
hypotheses:
Let $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$ be a morphism of sites
given by a continuous functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$.
Let $q$ be a point of $\mathcal{D}$ given by the functor
$v : \mathcal{D} \to \textit{Sets}$, see
Definition \ref{definition-point}.
conclusions:
the functor $v \circ u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
defines a point $p$ of $\mathcal{C}$ and moreover there is
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.

reason: The first of two explicit proofs shows v∘u meets the cover and overlap conditions for a point by continuity. The stalk identity follows from f^{-1}=u_s and the previous left-Kan-extension stalk formula; exactness of the composite inverse-image functors gives the remaining point axiom. A second alternative proof appears at lines 8593–8636.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
be a morphism of topoi. Let $q : \Sh(pt) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be a point. Then $p = f \circ q$ is a point of the topos
$\Sh(\mathcal{C})$ and we have
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.
hypotheses:
Let $f : \Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$
be a morphism of topoi. Let $q : \Sh(pt) \to \Sh(\mathcal{D})$
be a point.
conclusions:
$p = f \circ q$ is a point of the topos
$\Sh(\mathcal{C})$ and we have
a canonical identification
$$
(f^{-1}\mathcal{F})_q = \mathcal{F}_p
$$
for any sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathcal{C}$.

reason: The composite of a given topos point q with the topos morphism f is a point by closure under composition; its inverse-image functor is q^{-1}f^{-1}, yielding the displayed stalk equality by definition.
